title: Date arithmetic in an invented calendar
prompt:
An invented calendar has these rules. A year has 10 months, numbered 1 to 10. Months 1 to 9 have 36 days each; month 10 has 41 days, or 42 days in a leap year. A year is a leap year if it is divisible by 6 but not by 90, or if it is divisible by 360 (so 6 and 360 are leap years, while 90 and 180 are not). Years are numbered from 1, and the days run on without gaps from one year to the next. A week has 6 days, named `Ari`, `Bel`, `Cor`, `Dun`, `Eld` and `Fen`, which repeat in this order; day 1 of month 1 of year 1 is an `Ari`. A date is written `YYYY-MM-DD`, with the year padded with zeros to 4 digits and the month and the day to 2 digits each. A date is valid only if its month is 1 to 10 and its day is between 1 and the number of days of that month in that year.
Answer the queries listed at the end in order, one line each:
- `ADD DATE n`: the date n days after DATE (n may be negative, meaning that many days before), followed by a space and its weekday, for example `0003-04-05 Bel`.
- `DIFF DATE1 DATE2`: the number of days from DATE1 to DATE2, negative if DATE2 is earlier.
- `NTH k WEEKDAY YYYY-MM`: the date of the k-th day named WEEKDAY in that month (k counts from 1), written like the answer of ADD; if the month has fewer than k such days, print `none`.
If a date in a query is not valid, or a month in an NTH query is not 1 to 10, print `invalid date` instead of the answer. No answer falls before year 1.
Queries, in order: ADD 0001-01-01 0; ADD 0359-10-40 3; ADD 0360-10-41 1; ADD 0450-03-17 -1000; DIFF 0090-10-41 0091-01-01; DIFF 0721-05-30 0001-01-01; ADD 0539-10-42 1; NTH 3 Dun 0540-07; NTH 7 Fen 0012-10; NTH 7 Ari 0013-10; DIFF 0180-10-42 0181-01-01; ADD 0002-01-01 -365; NTH 7 Bel 0013-10; ADD 0005-11-01 1; ADD 0359-01-01 365.
